counterweight_triage.concern: The progress watcher, prompt shaping, state derivation, completion proof, and retention logic are split across several modules.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The boundaries are cohesive: live observation is isolated in task_run_progress, runner-facing prompt and receipt assembly in task_run_lane_runner, pure state derivation in task_run_state, and proof/retention orchestration in task_run_completion.

counterweight_triage.concern: The bounded stderr tail can omit early phase markers.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The live watcher accumulates phases and completion merges guard-observed phases in canonical order; tests cover markers aging out of the tail.

counterweight_triage.concern: A gate-mutated but freshly committed candidate may have its worktree released despite approval denial.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The documentation explicitly permits release when a fresh complete commit carries the candidate even though proof denied approval, and the receipt remains ineligible.

findings.action: Pass the guard stop reason into apply_lane_receipt(), use it as the blocker when transcript parsing has none, and add an integration test covering failed marker persistence through completion, lane_progress, blockers, and next_step.
evidence: scripts/task_run/task_run_progress.py: LaneProgressWatch._run assigns stop_reason before calling fire(), and deliberately survives any exception from fire().
scripts/task_run/task_run_progress.py: LaneProgressWatch.fire() may fail to append NO-PROGRESS-STOP but still invokes the kill callback.
scripts/task_run/task_run_lane_runner.py: apply_lane_receipt() derives blocker only from parsed delivery/stderr and merges only guard phases; it does not accept or merge progress_guard.stop_reason.

tests/charness_cli/test_task_run_implementation_lane.py: test_watch_run_records_stop_before_failing_fire proves stop_reason survives a failed fire, but no completion-level test proves that this reason reaches lane_progress or blockers.

docs/agent-task-runs.md claims a guard-killed lane is recorded with a typed NO-PROGRESS-STOP blocker; the failure path instead retains the reason only under progress_guard and can produce merely a generic execution failure downstream.
findings.summary: A no-progress stop can lose its typed blocker from lane_progress and the actionable next step when appending the transcript marker fails.

next_move: Repair the missing stop-reason merge and add the completion-level regression test before approval; then rerun the focused task-run tests and declared Python/docs/package validators.
